correctness.rationale: For r≥2 positive equal-rate residents and one rare rate a(1−1/(2r)), homogeneity yields exact simplex map. With S=1−z, normalized residents u_i obey u_i′=u_i(1−Su_i/2)/(1−S∑u_i²/2). Exact bounds keep z≤M<1, and order-preserving contraction of resident spread gives E=∑(u_i−1/r)²=O(ρ^{2n}). The exact z drift forces extinction and 1/z=O(n); the inverse increment w′−w=c_r(1−z)/(1−z/2)−ε, c_r=(2r+1)/(2(2r−1)), ε≥0 summable because E/z=O(nρ^{2n}). Therefore w/n→c_r, z−1/(c_r n)=O(log n/n²), and summing the inverse increments gives w=c_r n−(1/2)log n+C+o(1). No boundary-zero initial composition or uniform rate is asserted. Independently checked the rational normalized, drift, and inverse identities for several r and iterated 60000 steps; checks support not replace the argument.
